To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface resistance of Nb is affected by the thickness of the Ti and Cu capping layers, which in turn impacts the microwave loss of flexible thin-films superconducting microstriplines.

1) Ti/Nb bilayers increase surface resistance by up to 10% and Nb/Cu bilayers increase surface by up to 30%, 2) these bilayers increase surface roughness by up to 50% and 3) these bilayers decrease the critical temperature by 0.1 K.
we investigated how different thicknesses (10 nm and 50 nm), used as an under-layer for adhesion, impact the losses of thin-film superconductor microstrip resonators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, and characterization of flexible superconducting niobium (Nb) microstrip resonators on a 20-μ m-thick polyimide ( PI-2611 ) substrate.
the development and characterization of flexible superconducting transmission line resonator devices.
the development of a superconducting flexible cable that can be used for the transmission of low-noise signals at cryogenic temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 20 nm Ti underlayer and a 20 nm Cu capping layer are the optimal stack-up for a Nb-based superconducting micro-strip line on flexible polyimide substrates.
the Ti/Nb bilayer structure and Nb/Cu bilayer structure are not suitable as signal traces on a flexible superconducting transmission line.
we can use the data from our experiments to conclude that the best choice for the conductor stack-up in our case is a Nb signal trace with no under-layer and a 200-nm-thick Cu capping layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the use of Ti/Nb and Nb/Cu bilayers in superconducting micro-strip resonator structures can lead to an increase in conductor loss.

the RF loss of Nb signal traces on flexible polyimide substrates is not significantly impacted by the presence of a Ti adhesion layer, but that a Cu capping layer can increase the surface resistance of Nb and thus increase the loss.
the use of a thin Ti under-layer and a thick Cu capping layer are not recommended when fabricating superconducting Nb microstrip resonators on flexible polyimide substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Ti and Cu layers can increase conductor loss and, thus, degrade the quality of superconducting microresonators.
the use of a Ti under-layer for adhesion purposes should be avoided, and a Cu capping layer should be used to protect the Nb signal trace.
the use of Ti and Cu layers in the conductor stack-up can lead to increased microwave loss in flexible Nb superconductor microstrip resonators.
